subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should the repository approve this grouped set of 14 upstream action revisions for workflows that receive secrets, mint tokens, publish images, run security scans, and execute Codex agents?
rationale: Source review can confirm the OpenClaw YAML is pin-only, but accepting new third-party executable revisions at credential boundaries requires explicit repository security and workflow-owner trust.

options.title: Approve after exact-head proof
options.body: Verify each sensitive upstream revision and require refreshed exact-head security, CodeQL, token, Codex, and container-publish workflow evidence before merging the grouped update.

options.title: Split sensitive updates
options.body: Separate token, Codex, CodeQL, and publishing actions from routine setup-action bumps so each security boundary can be reviewed and validated independently.

options.title: Pause the refresh
options.body: Leave the existing immutable pins in place until Dependabot access and exact-head validation are reliable enough to review the batch safely.

recommendation.title: Approve after exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Verify each sensitive upstream revision and require refreshed exact-head security, CodeQL, token, Codex, and container-publish workflow evidence before merging the grouped update.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent release, workflow, and security history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for accepting third-party action revisions at credential boundaries.
